title: gpu-oom-debug-notes-maya-thompson
content:
Context:
- Working on reproducer for intermittent GPU OOM seen in production on dedicated nodes (p4d.24xlarge-ish).
- Errors only occur for long context windows (>8k tokens) and multicore batching.
- Suspect mix of fragmentation + driver/lib mismatch after driver update in late Jan.

Quick repro steps (devbox):
1) checkout branch: git checkout fix/kv-cache-fragmentation
2) build wheel: tox -e py38 -- setup bdist_wheel
3) run minimal repro: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python repro/run_long_context.py --model redwood/open-8k --batch 4 --ctx 12000 --iters 5

Commands and outputs collected:
- nvidia-smi (on failing host)
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  | NVIDIA-SMI 555.92.01    Driver Version: 555.92.01    CUDA Version: 12.1     |
  | GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
  |  0  A100-SXM4-40GB     On   | 00000000:3E:00.0 Off |                  N/A |
  |  0%   89C    P0   400W / 400W |   40960MiB / 40960MiB |  0%   0%   0%          |
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
- python stderr from failing run:
  "terminate called after throwing an instance of 'thrust::system_error'
  what():  cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory"
- trace (from logcat-like trace in app):
  2026-02-21T03:12:47Z - request id=ea3b - batch_size=8 ctx=12288 tokens_in=10240 tokens_out=2048
  allocate_kv_cache(size=~18.5GB) -> cudaMalloc failed (out of memory)
  fallback: try_to_free_cache() -> freed 2.2GB (prefix cache) but still insufficient
  attempt eviction -> fragmentation prevents contiguous allocation -> OOM

Hypotheses so far:
- H1: Memory fragmentation due to repeated allocate/free of KV caches + different sequence lengths -> large contiguous allocation fails even if summed free memory > request.
- H2: Driver / CUDA runtime mismatch: host driver reports CUDA 12.1 but container runtime uses CUDA 11.8 libs -> allocator behavior changes, cuBLAS/cuDNN ABI subtle differences leading to extra reserved memory.
- H3: Batching policy causing sudden large simultaneous KV allocs when micro-batches align (rare), amplified by prefetch/cache heuristics.
- H4: Quantization kernel (custom fused ops) doing temporary workspace allocations that are not accounted for in the model-only memory estimate.

Notes from system inspection:
- ldconfig in container shows libcuda from host mounted: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 -> 555.92.01 (matches host)
- /usr/local/cuda -> points to CUDA 11.8 in container image (mismatch with driver-reported CUDA 12.1)
- torch.cuda.version: 11.8 (from pip torch build)
- cuBLAS/cuDNN versions: cudnn 8.4 (container), cublas shipped with torch wheel (unknown minor)
- output of env (relevant):
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
  LD_PRELOAD=
  LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64:/opt/conda/lib

Repro attempts and results:
- Increase swap (not ideal): sudo fallocate -l 64G /swapfile && mkswap && swapon -> does not prevent OOM (cudaMalloc still fails).
- Run with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 -> same OOM but stack more deterministic (good for debugging).
- Force defragmentation via small alloc/free loop before request:
    python -c "import torch; x=[torch.empty(1024*1024, device='cuda') for _ in range(30)]; del x"
  -> slight improvement but still hit OOM in long runs. Suggests fragmentation partial but not full fix.
- Reduced batch size from 8->4 -> eliminates OOM in majority of runs (consistent with aggregate memory pressure hypothesis).
- Upgraded libnvidia-ml and remounted host libs (experimental) -> intermittent difference, sometimes OOM disappears for a day then returns.

Error snippets observed in different runs:
- cublas runtime error: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED when launching matmul for attention (only on some processes)
- NCCL WARN: non peer accessible memory / no p2p -> unrelated but captured concurrently
- dmesg on host shows no oom_kill; only "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3E:00): 31" on some nodes -> Xid 31 indicates a GPU page fault / illegal memory access (could be driver bug)

Instrumentation to add:
- Track contiguous free block sizes: add helper in allocator to scan free list and log largest_free_contiguous_bytes at allocation time.
- Log sequence length distribution per request and per worker (histograms).
- Add safe fallback: if contiguous block not available, try multiple smaller allocations and migrate to pinned host tensor (slower) instead of immediate OOM.
- Add telemetry tag when driver/installed-cuda-version mismatch detected.

Potential mitigations to test (priority order):
1) Conservative default: limit max_batch_tokens per worker and add soft guard for kv_allocation > 70% of GPU memory -> reject or stream. (Low risk)
2) Rebuild runtime wheel against host CUDA 12.1 toolchain to ensure full ABI parity (medium effort, high impact).
3) Implement allocator defrag routine between large requests (coalesce free blocks) - tricky and may impact latency.
4) Add pre-allocation for worst-case KV cache for pinned endpoints to avoid fragmentation (reserve contiguous chunk on startup).

Notes for follow-ups / playbook updates:
- If Xid 31 observed, escalate to infra + driver team, include nvidia-smi -q -x output and /var/log/nvidia-installer.log.
- Add a job in CI that runs long-context e2e on a smaller GPU to catch regressions (8k tokens, batch 4, 50 iters).
- Update runbooks: how to detect driver/CUDA mismatch (ldconfig vs nvcc --version vs torch.cuda.version) and immediate mitigations (scale down batch, restart runtime after full driver upgrade).

Loose TODOs:
- [ ] Add contiguous_free metric + expose in /metrics endpoint.
- [ ] Reproduce on an isolated node with full host container build (CUDA 12.1).
- [ ] Open issue to vendor for possible Xid 31 driver bug (include repro script).
- [ ] Try using CUB allocator override (jemalloc-like strategy) in toy harness.

Notes to self (quick hits):
- When debugging locally use: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 python repro/run_long_context.py --batch 4 --ctx 12000
- Keep experiments reproducible: always record git sha + docker image tag (I forgot yesterday and wasted time).

End of notes.
